intro.text: Birds with special powers, such as Kokerlii, whose power hides the trapper Dusk's boat from a creature under the water on his way into the Pantheon.

Birds that gained powers, called talents, on Patji, an island of First of the Sun, and can share them with people. Birds from outside the Pantheon can become Aviar too, by visiting Patji and eating the fruit of Cakoban's fingers.

description.text: Most Aviar are fairly large birds, about three fists tall, though some kinds are smaller or bigger. Their looks vary from species to species, in reds, greens, blacks, blues and whites, sometimes mixed. Some have sharp talons and hooked beaks like a raptor's. Young Aviar can barely fly, but healthy adults fly well unless their wings are clipped.

They are cleverer than ordinary animals, though in the wild they act like any bird, gathering in flocks, roosting in trees and building nests to lay eggs and raise chicks. Long single feathers called mating plumes, usually found near nests, play some part in their mating. Their powers give them a measure of protection from predators, but they flee quickly when startled. They eat fresh fruit, and also seeds, dried fruit and fish.
Each species usually lives on one particular island. They can be moved to the homeisles without trouble, but wild Aviar live only in the Pantheon.

Each has its own personality: Kokerlii is cheerful and oblivious, whereas Sak is far more guarded. They appear to grasp some human speech and respond to their owner's commands and other sounds. A few can imitate sounds, and certain trappers can tell what they feel and intend. They can be trained in particular behaviours, such as coming back when their owner whistles, or even attacking other animals.

items.text: Throughout First of the Sun's history, Aviar were found only in the Pantheon. Its people recorded the birds and their powers carefully, and centuries passed with no new kind discovered. The birds feature in folk tales, such as that of Linji, who tried to circle the globe by sea with no Aviar.

Trappers knew the birds best. They trained hard to survive on the islands, where they thought nothing of killing one another, and were bound by tradition and reverent towards the islands, Patji most of all. Famously reticent and stubborn, they kept what they knew about the Aviar and their powers to themselves.

Only trappers had ever brought Aviar out of the Pantheon. Trading companies long hoped to set up on the islands to breed and sell the birds, but trappers refused to help, and deepwalkers and other deadly animals defeated every company expedition, so Aviar stayed fairly scarce in the homeisles. After the Ones Above arrived, the companies quickly built new technology such as propeller-driven warships, which gave the Northern Interests Trading Company the nerve to launch the Patji expedition.

On the expedition, Vathi, a scientist and explorer working for the company, befriended the trapper Sixth of the Dusk and learned things about the islands and the Aviar that the public had never known. These discoveries, which overturned centuries of Eelakin belief, shocked her.

Among the devices the company had from the Ones Above was one that could find Aviar on an island. When staff switched it on on Patji, the Aviar grew agitated and lost their powers. Dusk and Vathi realized that the Ones Above wanted the birds but were somehow forbidden to take them from a less advanced people, and were quietly speeding up First of the Sun's industry to get around that rule. The two vowed to stop them.

The Ones Above pushed for Patji to be turned into a settlement for breeding Aviar. Much of its dangerous wildlife was culled, roads and other works were built for easier access, and vast aviaries went up to raise the birds in great numbers.

Each species of bird gains a different power. Some powers work on their own, while others have to be switched on by the Aviar, sometimes when a bonded person asks. The powers are usually very reliable, though a strange device that the Ones Above gave to the Northern Interests Trading Company disrupted them.

Young birds gain their talents by eating special worms that live on Patji, and Aviar from across the Pantheon travel there to get one. The worms infest fruit dropped by the Cakoban's fingers that grow beside Patji's Eye, and the birds swallow them along with the fruit. Birds not native to the Pantheon rarely develop such powers.
The talents come from a partnership with the worms, which are Invested; once eaten, they give the bird powers that depend on its species.
An Aviar does not need to keep eating worms for its talent to keep working, since the birds are often shipped to the far-off homeisles. Trappers have found that only young birds gain talents.
Most people are bonded to a single Aviar, though some trappers keep bonds with three or more at once.

An Aviar shares its power with a person through a bond of the spirit. The bond is not especially strong, which lets it be moved from one person to another at will. It links minds, too: Dusk speaks of Sak sending him her visions. An Aviar can sense where its bonded person is, and some can lend their talents to people other than their usual owner. Sharing a talent does not require a fully formed bond.

Some form of this talent seems common, since flocks of wild Aviar can hide from predators that hunt by sensing minds, such as nightmaws. Herds of grazing animals sleep near Aviar roosts to shelter under the shield the birds provide.
Streamers, green and white birds, are one breed that can hide minds.
Five known breeds of Aviar can hide minds, streamers among them.

The Aviar can hide its own mind and those of others nearby. It can let the shield drop, and can let chosen beings in while keeping the rest out. Holding the shield for long periods does not seem to tire the bird, but it weakens with distance from the Aviar.

This talent lets a bird see the ways a person might die and show them as visions of corpses wherever those deaths could happen, sometimes dozens at once. The deaths shown may be minutes or years away.
Sak, a raven brought from outside the Pantheon, is the only Aviar known to have this talent; other ravens taken there gained a different one.

A corpse can stand for an immediate physical threat, often bearing the wound it would cause, or for a vaguer, more abstract danger. The Aviar can tint the corpses in different shades to signal how great the danger is, and when a threat passes they slowly fade.

Only those the Aviar chooses to share its talent with can see the corpses. The bird can switch the talent on or off at will, and using it for long tires it. It can show the visions to others, including the corpses of people it is not bonded to, and other Aviar may be able to see them as well.
A bright red kind of Aviar lets those bonded to it see colours they normally cannot.

Aviar raised by someone from hatching bond with that person and like to stay close, treating them as part of the flock, and birds a trapper has raised together usually get along. They often enjoy an affectionate scratch, show displeasure with a gentle nip, and find the soft click of a tongue soothing. In safecamps they live happily in nesting boxes, and trappers let them come and go as they please without worrying that they will not return.

Because the Pantheon is so deadly, only trappers, highly trained outdoorsmen, can survive there and raise the birds. Each trapper settles on one island and comes to know its species best, keeping Aviar as companions and breeding and selling them for a living.
